payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING calls-media-1 (high/authz, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/calls/call-control-plane.ts
LINES: 464-516

WHAT: sfuProduce/sfuConsume/sfuConnectTransport authorize via #requireSfuParticipant (lines 493-516), which only verifies the actor is SOME joined participant of the live call — it never checks that the supplied transportId/producerId belongs to the actor. The SFU backends store transports at router/call granularity with no participant binding: FakeSfuBackend produce()/consume() only check `router.transports.has(input.transportId)` (fake-sfu-backend.ts 149-186) and MediasoupSfuBackend #requireTransport only looks up by callId+transportId (mediasoup-sfu-backend.ts 182-218, 307-313). transportIds are server-assigned but returned to clients in join grants and are also enumerable. So joined participant B can pass participant A's transportId to sfuProduce (inject media that the SFU attributes to A's transport) or sfuConnectTransport (complete/Hijack A's DTLS handshake), and sfuConsume lets any participant consume any producerId on the router.

IMPACT: Cross-participant media spoofing and tampering inside a call: B can produce tracks on A's transport (impersonate A's media), disrupt A's DTLS state, and consume arbitrary producers. Breaks per-participant media integrity even though call-level membership is enforced.

SUGGESTED FIX: Bind each created transport (and producer) to a (userId,deviceId) at createWebRtcTransport/produce time, persist that ownership in the backend, and have connectTransport/produce assert the transport's owner == actor and consume assert the recv transport's owner == actor. The verifyJoinToken from calls-token-1 should carry the same identity to cross-check.
